h1: IRabbit Hotel Prachinburi — a minimalist-design hotel in the town centre, where the rooms are clean and the market is a walk away
intro: If you're in Prachinburi for business or to explore the town and want a clean, design-led room on a few-hundred to low-thousand baht budget — IRabbit Hotel is a name Prachinburi travellers keep mentioning. It's a 3-star minimalist-style hotel on Chaeng Pattana Road, Na Muang, opened in 2017 with 59 rooms. The draw is its town-centre location within walking distance of the night market and the public park, plus rooms that real reviews praise for cleanliness and friendly service. Rates start at about ฿700/night, rising into the low thousands for king rooms or long weekends.

body.html: The heart of IRabbit Hotel is its town-centre location, within walking distance of the food and sights in central Prachinburi. The hotel sits on Chaeng Pattana Road, Na Muang, about 600 m from the Prachinburi night market and 550 m from Prachin Wanarom public park. It's near the provincial sports centre, convenience stores, petrol stations and several walkable restaurants. For anyone here on business, government errands, or exploring the town without a car, it's far handier than a hillside resort you have to drive out to.

The hotel itself is a minimalist-design building that looks new and uncluttered. There are 59 rooms split between Standard King rooms and Standard Twin rooms (around 24 sq m). Inside you get air-con, a TV, a fridge and a minibar, with some rooms adding a sitting balcony. What real reviews agree on is that rooms are clean, a good size, with comfy beds and decor that feels more modern than the older hotels in town - good value for a few hundred to a thousand-odd baht.
"New, fresh, stylish rooms, good staff service, right in town with the market in walking distance - perfect for a one-night stopover or a trip into town on business."

The facilities are solid for this level of hotel. There's free on-site parking, a 24-hour front desk, plus a security guard and CCTV. There's a small restaurant and bar, a garden and sitting terrace, and a bicycle-rental service for pedalling around town. Breakfast is served roughly 7-10 am - it's made to order, with bread and coffee at the counter and an inexpensive buffet option. It isn't a grand spread, but it's an easy way to start the day.

The in-town location is also handy for onward sightseeing. It's about a 15-minute drive to the Abhaibhubejhr hospital and Thai herbal-medicine museum, a Prachinburi landmark. From here you can carry on towards the Prachinburi side of Khao Yai, or the Noen Hom area, without a long drive. Anyone using this as a base for a night in town before moving on to Khao Yai or Kabin Buri can plan it neatly.

To be honest about a couple of things worth knowing before you book: the rates here run a touch higher than the plainer hotels in the province. Some reviewers note that comparable places in the same bracket sit around 700-800 baht, though here you trade up for the design and cleanliness. There's also a deposit of about 500 baht taken at check-in, refunded at check-out. And because it's a town hotel rather than a resort, there's no pool or spa - if you're after a full nature setting, this isn't that kind of place.

Overall, IRabbit Hotel earns high real-review scores on Trip.com, especially for cleanliness, staff service, and its in-town location. Rates start around ฿700 for a standard room, rising into the low thousands for a king room or a long weekend. If you want an in-town hotel that's clean, design-led, and within walking distance of the market and park on a modest budget, this place hits the mark.

A tip from following the reviews here: for a comfortable, quiet night, ask for a room that doesn't face the main road, and if you're here to eat well in town, walk over to the night market in the evening since it's only about 600 m away. Book ahead over long weekends, as in-town hotels with rooms this good fill up fast.

If you're watching the price against other hotels in the province - rates are a touch higher than the plainer options and there's a 500-baht deposit -> for the cheapest in-town option, look at Jiphome or Peamsuk Sweet instead.
If you're mainly here for rafting or nature - the hotel is in the town centre, far from the rafting run and Khao Yai -> to sleep by the activities, consider Wangtaparb Resort in the Na Di area.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — IRabbit Hotel Prachinburi

faq.q: Where is IRabbit Hotel in Prachinburi, and what's nearby?
faq.a: IRabbit Hotel is at 54 Chaeng Pattana Road, Na Muang, Mueang District, Prachinburi. It's a town-centre hotel within walking distance of the Prachinburi night market (~600 m), Prachin Wanarom public park (~550 m) and the provincial sports centre. It's about a 15-minute drive to the Abhaibhubejhr hospital and museum.

faq.q: How much does IRabbit Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿700/night for a Standard Twin. Choices run from Standard Twin and Standard King to Deluxe and family rooms. Prices rise into the low thousands for bigger rooms or long weekends - always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at IRabbit Hotel?
faq.a: Rooms are minimalist in design, with air-con, a TV, a fridge, a minibar, and some with a balcony. Twin rooms are around 24 sq m. Real reviews praise clean, good-sized rooms with comfy beds and decor that feels more modern than the older hotels in town.

faq.q: Does IRabbit Hotel have parking and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes to both. There's free on-site parking, a 24-hour front desk, plus a security guard and CCTV. Breakfast is served roughly 7-10 am, made to order with bread and coffee plus an inexpensive buffet option. There's also a bicycle-rental service for getting around town.

faq.q: Who is IRabbit Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for anyone here on business or government errands, or exploring the town without a car, who wants a clean, design-led room on a modest budget. It also works as a base for a night in town before moving on to Khao Yai or Kabin Buri. But if you want a nature setting or a hillside resort, this is a town hotel with no pool or spa.

faq.q: Does IRabbit Hotel take a deposit?
faq.a: Yes. The hotel takes a deposit of about 500 baht at check-in, refunded at check-out. Keep cash or a card handy. Note too that room rates can be a touch higher than the plainer hotels in the province, traded off against the better design and cleanliness.
